text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE

- Three unknown persons riddled with bullets the car of former foreign minister Alfred Serreqi, who split with President Sali Berisha's Democrats. Serreqi said the attackers were angry at his critical remarks of Berisha.
- Italian police seized 1.94 tonnes of marijuana in a truck near Milan. It is believed the drug shipment had come from Albania.

- The existence of salvation committees in the south remains a bone of contention between the two main parties, the Democrats and the Socialists, threatening the holding of a general election by the end of June.
- A Council of Europe delegation warned Albania they had to choose either elections or chaos.
- Schools re-opened in the southern town of Vlore protected by armed guards but only 30 percent of the pupils showed up for the first day.

- A heavily-armed gang operating near the northern town of Shkoder organised the shipment of more than a thousand people to Italy. It added Italian vessels were patrolling the area to avoid other ships from leaving.
- The soccer federation is thinking of re-starting the soccer championship it was forced to suspend three months ago.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE

- A Council of Europe mission said President Berisha was the only one who did not believe in a compromise over a proposed electoral law, adding that political parties should try to convince him to change his mind.
- The European delegation said they would propose an electoral law if the Albanian parties did not reach a consensus within the week.
- Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi has urged President Berisha and Prime Minister Bashkim Fino to hold elections in June.
- A Democratic Party leader, Genc Pollo, said the main obstacle to holding elections was the presence of armed committees in the south of the country.
- A Tirana court will begin the trials of the managers of four failed pyramid schemes within days.

- Vehbi Alimucaj, the owner of one of the country's biggest concern which also runs a high interest money scheme, has accused the former governor of the central bank, Kristaq Luniku, of being a barrier to economic development by not licensing a private Albanian bank.
ALBANIA

- The paper alleges a criminal from the southern port city of Vlore gave the profits he made from people fleeing Albania by ship to Finance Minister Arben Malaj so that he could pay pensioners in Vlore.
- Prime Minister Fino has deceived a Council of Europe delegation by saying there are only two salvation committees in Albania. The paper claims there are five more such commitees.
- Three young men were killed after an unknown gunman opened fire while they were playing snooker.
- Defence Minister Shaqir Vukaj receives the highest salary of any official in Albania, 75,000 leks a month.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- A Council of Europe mission has stressed that so-called rebel committees in the south of Albania should be disbanded.
- Democratic Party leader Tritan Shehu has demanded the Socialists distance themselves from what it terms their armed rebel allies in the south.
- The paper says in an editorial the Democratic Party is walking towards a bigger victory now that the silent majority of Albanians are wakening after a winter of terror.
